description: core §3.3, the compact descriptor. Written by an independent reading of the text (Python, standard library), checked by a second, never blessed. `revisions` holds each revision the cases read, by name: its authoring file (relative to this directory), its interface and fingerprint, its resources in the canonical form's order (§9.5) with the bits one takes, ⌈log₂ n⌉ for n resources, the capabilities it gates on, sorted bytewise, and its `uses`. `catalogs` holds three deployment catalogs (§8.6): `first`; `second`, which succeeds it, and lists `ghost.v1` at a fingerprint no revision has; and `other`, apart. `ids` gives each one's id. A value is a descriptor, its envelope's seq and its `minted` bit. `writes`: a value and the catalog its owner holds → the payload's bytes in hex and their count. `reads`: a payload, the instance key it came on, the catalogs a reader holds and the revisions it lacks (`lacks`, none when absent; it holds every other) → the value, or the refusal's token, the first in §3.3's order. A decoded descriptor's `token` is written out, and an empty member left out. Every accepted read writes back to its bytes under the catalog its descriptor names, read through what the case holds.
